title: FDA premarket SBOM supplement (DERIVED)
description: DERIVED from prose, not published by FDA. FDA asks for a machine-readable SBOM consistent with the NTIA minimum elements (October 2021 'Framing Software Component Transparency') and, for each software component, two additional elements, which 'manufacturers may choose to provide ... as part of the SBOM, or ... separately, such as in an addendum' (Sec. V.A.4(b)); plus all known vulnerabilities with a safety and security risk assessment and risk controls (Sec. V.A.4(b)). This schema models the addendum form. Constrained by fda-premarket-cybersecurity-guidance#V.A.4.b-01..13, #VII.C.3-01..02, #VII.D.2-09..10.

device.description: Device and version the SBOM describes. Devices should be electronically and visibly identifiable (App. 1 D, e.g. UDI, model number, serial number).

sbom_reference.description: The machine-readable SBOM this addendum supplements. FDA encourages industry-accepted formats but names none; SPDX and CycloneDX are examples of such formats, not FDA's.

justification_if_not_provided.description: If a manufacturer is unable to provide the SBOM information to FDA, the manufacturer should provide a justification (V.A.4.b-07). For cyber devices the SBOM is required by statute (524B(b)(3)), so this field cannot substitute for it.

component_ref.description: Identifier of the component inside the referenced SBOM (e.g. SPDX element id, CycloneDX bom-ref, or purl).

origin.description: Sec. V.A.4(a)/VII.C.3 vocabulary: manufacturer-developed ('proprietary'), purchased/licensed (commercial), open-source, off-the-shelf.

level_of_support.description: 'The software level of support provided through monitoring and maintenance from the software component manufacturer (e.g., the software is actively maintained, no longer maintained, abandoned)' (V.A.4.b-03). FDA's values are examples (e.g.), so the enum is open via 'other'.

end_of_support_date.description: 'The software component’s end-of-support date.' (V.A.4.b-04). 'unknown' is our addition for components whose supplier publishes none; FDA states no rule for that case.

device_level_vulnerabilities.description: Known vulnerabilities 'associated with the device' that are not attributable to one component (V.A.4.b-08).

identifier.description: FDA names no scheme; CVE id where one exists is the obvious choice (our inference).

in_cisa_kev.description: Identified in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (V.A.4.b-08). KEV entries 'should be designed out of the device' (V.A.2-06).

discovery_method.description: How the vulnerability was discovered, 'to demonstrate whether the assessment methods were sufficiently robust' (V.A.4.b-09).

risk_assessment.description: 'A safety and security risk assessment of each known vulnerability (including device and system impacts)' (V.A.4.b-11).

risk_controls.description: Details of applicable safety and security risk controls (V.A.4.b-12).

compensating_controls.description: Described 'in an appropriate level of detail' when risk controls include them (V.A.4.b-13). App. 5: external to the device design, configurable in the field, employed by a user.
